$comment: Processes matching ANY rule below are NEVER candidates for kill, even
if they are reparented to PID 1 / user-systemd and have no controlling
tty. Scope: per-user cleanup tool. System.slice processes are filtered
out earlier (the reaper only inspects user.slice/user-1000.slice).
Rule semantics (UNION — match any one to be protected):
comm_substring      /proc/PID/comm contains an entry as substring
Sources for each rule come from live evidence on this host (Plasma 6 +
pipewire + KDE + WireGuard + git ssh ControlMaster). Adding entries is
data-driven: edit this JSON, no script change needed.
$comment_exe: Why this list is narrow: '/nix/store/' would match every bash and
every nix-built binary, which is ~all user processes — useless as a
protection rule. Use comm and cgroup for general protection. Reserve
exe_substring for specific binaries only (none currently — comm/argv
rules above + cgroup_substring below cover the live evidence).
$notes_app_slice: We deliberately DO NOT whitelist /user@1000.service/app.slice/ as a
blanket rule. App-slice cgroups carry the @<UUID>.service tag of the
konsole/brave/etc. instance that spawned them; if the parent app is
closed the cgroup becomes a ghost holding leaked children. The exe and
comm rules above already protect live instances of those apps. A leaked
esbuild --watch=forever sitting in a closed-konsole's app-slice cgroup
matches no rule above and is correctly killable.
